name: Hologram AI kernel
purpose: Decides what Hologram AI may load and run. A request names one decision in its first byte and carries that decision's numbers; the answer is the verdict. Nine decisions: whether a model may proceed (2), whether a stage plan is right (3), the quantisation tier (4), whether a buffer is admitted (5), whether a tensor's byte range is valid (6), whether a trim of the conversation is right (7), the next attention cache size (8), a turn's token budget (9) and the size a dimension is bound to (11). Anything else answers invalid request.

promise.headline: Admits a buffer exactly when its label and its length are the ones expected.
promise.detail: A buffer's label is the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes. The kernel compares all 32 bytes of the expected and observed labels and the declared and observed lengths, and admits only when every one is equal.

claim: KN-05: a buffer is admitted exactly when its expected and observed labels are equal and its declared and observed lengths are equal.

proposition.name: Admitted
proposition.text:
Admitted claim :=
  SameLabel claim.expected claim.observed
  /\ claim.declaredLength = claim.observedLength

SameLabel left right :=
  left.w0 = right.w0 /\ left.w1 = right.w1 /\ left.w2 = right.w2 /\ left.w3 = right.w3
proposition.plain: The observed label is the expected label, word for word, and the observed length is the declared length.

theorems.name: admitted_decides
theorems.statement: Kernel.Admission::admitted claim = true ↔ Admitted claim, for every claim
theorems.how: Proved by simplification over the record fields, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: within_decides
theorems.statement: Kernel.Range::within fileLength previousEnd offset length = true ↔ previousEnd ≤ offset ∧ offset + length ≤ fileLength, for every four numbers
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: all_accepted_ordered
theorems.statement: allAccepted fileLength previousEnd spans = true ↔ Ordered fileLength previousEnd spans, for every list of ranges
theorems.how: Proved by induction over the list, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: grow_bounds
theorems.statement: needed ≤ maximum ∧ current ≤ maximum → needed ≤ grow ∧ grow ≤ maximum ∧ current ≤ grow, for every three numbers
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: budget_within_context
theorems.statement: used < context → used + budget ≤ context ∧ 1 ≤ budget, for every three numbers
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: budget_within_request
theorems.statement: 0 < requested → budget ≤ requested, for every three numbers
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: authorised_decides
theorems.statement: authorised = true ↔ no key missing ∧ no unsupported feature ∧ the manifest fits, for every four flags
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: tier_monotone
theorems.statement: budget ≤ larger → tier at budget ≤ tier at larger, for every parameter count
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: bind_bounds
theorems.statement: requested ≤ upper → requested ≤ bind ∧ bind ≤ upper, for every step
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: trimmed_decides
theorems.statement: trimmed = true ↔ what remains fits the context ∧ (anything dropped → restoring the newest dropped pair passes the context), for every five totals
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI

theorems.name: planned_decides
theorems.statement: planned = true ↔ the stage fits ∧ one more layer does not, unless it is the whole model ∧ the stages cover every layer, for every six numbers
theorems.how: Proved by linear arithmetic, checked by the Lean kernel by lexlean verify in CI
